ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the figure is a schematic diagram of port distribution in part of North America, marking the approximately 50°N latitude line and meridians such as 110°W and 80°W. Port b is located on the west coast of North America, along the Pacific coast; port c is located in the eastern part of the North American interior, near the Great Lakes; port d is located on the east coast of North America, along the Atlantic coast. Then reason: the freezing period of a port is mainly affected by winter temperature and oceanic influence. Port c is deep in the continental interior, with strong continentality in winter, obvious cooling, and the lake area is prone to freezing, so the freezing period is the longest. Port d is located on the east coast and is affected by high-latitude cold air and cold currents in winter; the temperature is relatively low and the freezing period is relatively long, but the oceanic moderating effect is stronger than that of inland port c. Port b is located on the west coast and is affected by the Pacific maritime climate and warm currents, so winter is relatively mild and the freezing period is the shortest. Therefore, the order of the freezing periods of ports b, c, and d from long to short is c>d>b.
